claims_and_limits: Published October 22 in Scientific Reports as an early accepted peer-reviewed article subject to later editing.

The authors report an average Chattering Index reduction exceeding 76% for both joints of a planar rehabilitation robot against hysteresis mitigation in comparative simulations while retaining tracking accuracy.
Neither physical hardware operation nor human or clinical outcomes are established. Hardware test criteria are editorial assessment.

visual.central_question: How should a team test the moment its robot controller changes modes?
visual.shared_motif: Generic two-joint arm and copper motion ribbon; conceptual contact, not a depiction of the study apparatus or human test.
visual.infographic_argument: Switching between admittance and impedance, filtering rapid changes, and measuring chattering with tracking are separate engineering checks.
visual.status: Conceptual artwork. The panel's squiggle is an illustrative icon, not a measured signal. Simulation and hardware boundary stated on image. Cover, 260px card and OG crop reviewed.
